title: Most People Miss This About The Serpent’s Strategy
paragraphs: Most People Miss This About The Serpent’s Strategy
He never starts with the fruit.

That’s the serpent’s strategy in Eden. Not fangs first. Not force first. A question first: “Did God really say…?” (Genesis 3:1). He did not begin by denying God outright. He began by bending the conversation, making Eve stare at the one boundary instead of the thousand gifts. That is how hell still whispers. It shifts your eyes from God’s goodness to God’s restriction.
And many people still miss it.

The serpent’s deepest weapon was not just temptation. It was suspicion. He wanted Eve to believe that obedience was loss, that God was withholding, that holiness was oppression, that freedom lived outside the will of God. That lie is still preaching today. “You’re missing out.” “You deserve more.” “God is too strict.” “Just this once.”

Before Adam and Eve ever touched the fruit, they had already begun doubting the Father. Sin usually enters through a cracked view of God. When God’s heart is questioned, God’s word becomes negotiable. And when God’s word becomes negotiable, desire takes the wheel.

That is the serpent’s strategy:
distort God’s words,
discredit God’s heart,
then drag you toward disobedience that looks beautiful for one moment and deadly for generations.

James says each person is tempted when he is lured and enticed by his own desire, and desire when it has conceived gives birth to sin, and sin brings forth death (James 1:14–15). The enemy knows this. He packages rebellion like wisdom. He makes poison sparkle.

Where Adam fell, Christ stood. Where the serpent twisted words, Jesus answered, “It is written” (Matthew 4:4). The first Adam reached for what was forbidden. The last Adam obeyed the Father completely. And through His cross, Jesus crushed the ancient serpent’s victory over sinners like us (Genesis 3:15; Colossians 2:15).

So the answer is not just “try harder.”
The answer is see God rightly.
Trust His heart.
Stand on His word.
Run to Christ.

Because the serpent still whispers,
but the Savior still saves.

And maybe that is the word for somebody today: the battle is not only over your behavior. It is over your belief about who God is. He is not starving you. He is shepherding you. He is not ruining your joy. He is protecting your soul.
